$comment: Passing this schema is a structural result, not a semantic one. Draft 2020-12 cannot express ten published rules, so a validated payload may still be refused by the Python constructors: uniqueness over items[*].constraint.stable_id, the equality of refinement_reason and explanation.reason, the metadata nesting bound, the digit limit on published integers, a duration inside the float range, non-finite numbers, values with no JSON counterpart, non-string object keys, a narrative step citing a member outside the core, and a review surface naming a member that cannot be edited. A consumer that needs those guarantees must check them separately.
title: PyFCSTM BMC CLI result
description: Structured BMC JSON envelope emitted by pyfcstm bmc --json.

allOf.$comment: An explanation names the work behind it, except when the budget refused to start anything: the frozen timeout boundary still requires that be reported, with an empty ledger.
Only the degraded statuses are excluded, matching the constructor.  A feasible scenario reporting complete with executed checks predates this contract.

refinement_reason.$comment: Draft 2020-12 cannot compare two arbitrary strings, so it cannot check that this equals explanation.reason; the constructor enforces that equality.

Only the degraded statuses are excluded, matching the constructor.  A feasible scenario reporting complete with executed checks predates this contract.
A published core claims some check proved its target unsatisfiable, so the ledger has to carry that completed check. Without it the JSON asserts soundness with no recorded evidence.
partial_minimized means at least one deletion check finished. With none recorded the core is simply raw.

Minimization publishes one aggregate phase record, so each reduction level maps to a ledger shape: raw has no record, partial_minimized has a degraded one, and proven has a completed one. Per-trial verdicts are steps inside the algorithm and never become rows -- a rule reading them as rows would reject a normal shrink, whose successful deletions come back unsat.

status=complete reports a whole phase rather than one solver verdict, so only phase-level checks may use it.  The branch below carries the list; naming them here as well would be a second place to keep in step, which is how this comment came to disagree with it.

Phases may report status=complete; a single solver verdict may not.  Core binding and proof construction join the phase family for the reason value propagation did: each aggregates several checks and supports a deeper tier rather than proving the core.

Added rather than replacing whatever pattern the field already carried -- those encode separate rules about the field's alphabet or prefix.

frames.$comment: Both the schema and the Python constructor accept a whole-valued 1.0 here and canonicalize it to 1, because a validator judging "integer" by numeric value cannot tell it from 1. The constructor additionally requires an array and refuses bool, fractional and negative entries, which this schema also refuses.

The constructor additionally requires an array and refuses bool, fractional and negative entries, which this schema also refuses.

refs.$comment: Same limits as normalized_fact: nesting depth, integer digit count, non-finite numbers, values with no JSON counterpart and non-string object keys are all outside Draft 2020-12 and are refused by the constructor.

source_excerpt.$comment: Bounded at 4096 Unicode code points so one long authored line cannot put an unbounded slice of the user's source into canonical JSON; the cut is declared through source_excerpt_truncated.

kind.$comment: A fact describes one source group. variable_comparison carries the relation in its operator field instead of splitting into a tag per relation. transition_case gives the assignment one step's selected case makes, under the condition that selects it; exactly one of operand and operand_variable is present, decided by whether the model wrote a literal or a variable. operation is add, sub, mul, div or set; set is a replacement rather than an arithmetic update -- the next frame's value does not depend on this one -- and the rules decline it because there is nothing to evaluate. proposition gives one requirement about one event at one step, carrying the identity the rule compares and the polarity the query asked for; a state assertion is not one of these and stays state_membership. Cross-group patterns -- incompatible equalities, an empty interval, an exhausted state domain, a value carried across a step, a definedness failure -- are derivations over several facts and are named by the narrative's rule vocabulary, never here. structural_constraint is the honest fallback for a shape no recognizer reads.

normalized_fact.$comment: Machine consumers dispatch on kind rather than on human text, so the tag is required.  Later stages extend the enum as recognizers land. Draft 2020-12 has no depth keyword, no way to bound an integer's digit count, and no way to see a non-finite number, a value with no JSON counterpart or a non-string object key -- a payload reaching a validator was already parsed from JSON text. The constructor refuses all of those at every nesting depth.

Added rather than replacing whatever pattern the field already carried -- those encode separate rules about the field's alphabet or prefix.

Added rather than replacing whatever pattern the field already carried -- those encode separate rules about the field's alphabet or prefix.

items.$comment: Members are ordered by constraint.stable_id and each id appears once. Draft 2020-12 cannot express uniqueness over a nested key, so uniqueItems covers identical members and the stable_id-level rule is enforced by BmcConflictCore plus its equivalence test.

proof.$comment: Null until the proof tier produces one.  The depth conditionals below decide which of the two applies.

reason.$comment: The constructor refuses whitespace-only text through one shared predicate, so the structural gate says the same with an added pattern; minLength alone lets a single space through.  Added rather than replacing whatever pattern the field already carried -- those encode separate rules about the field's alphabet or prefix.

elapsed_ms.$comment: Draft 2020-12 bounds a number's value, but an integer past the float range is still a legal JSON number; a duration has to be representable as one, so the constructor refuses it.

allOf.$comment: achieved_mode none means nothing publishable came back, so there is no core and therefore nothing for a narrative to describe -- its ids would reference a core that is not there. The constructor refuses the pairing and so does this branch.

narrative.$comment: A complete verdict needs a derivation that closed, not merely a narrative object. structural_only says outright that the conflict was not derived.

allOf.$comment: The frozen delivery truth table, exhaustively. The conditionals above report the common mistakes with a precise message, but their conjunction is weaker than the table: every one of them can hold while the combination appears in no authored row. Requesting 'none' matches no row, which is how the contract's explanation=None rule reads here.
Steps bind to proof nodes only in proof mode.  With no proof there are no nodes, so a citation points at something no artifact contains; the constructor refuses it and so does this branch.

span.$comment: Coordinates are 1-based and end-exclusive by producer contract. The source registry degrades any span it cannot slice to a null excerpt rather than rejecting it, so no bound is stated here; the constructor types these fields to match, which it previously did not.

reasoningStep.$comment: A step names the core members it reads so a consumer can jump from a sentence to the source lines behind it. Draft 2020-12 cannot require those ids to exist in core.items -- that is a relation between two sibling arrays, not a property of either -- so BmcInfeasibilityExplanation enforces it, together with the rule that a review surface names an editable member. Both are named semantic-gate exceptions.

item_ids.$comment: Ids go through the same predicate as the prose, so whitespace is refused here too; minLength alone lets a single space through.

proof_node_ids.$comment: Ids go through the same predicate as the prose, so whitespace is refused here too; minLength alone lets a single space through.

text.$comment: The constructor rejects whitespace-only text, and Draft 2020-12 can say the same with a pattern; minLength alone lets a single space through.

conflictNarrative.$comment: Rendered from the published core and its normalized facts alone: no file read, no solver. A shape with no domain reading yields structural_only and no conflict step rather than an invented chain. review_surfaces are authored entry points for review, not repair suggestions, and editing one is not a promise that the full target becomes satisfiable.

headline.$comment: Whitespace-only is refused by the constructor; a pattern says so here too.

summary.$comment: Whitespace-only is refused by the constructor; a pattern says so here too.

review_surfaces.$comment: Ids go through the same predicate as the prose, so whitespace is refused here too; minLength alone lets a single space through.

allOf.$comment: A complete derivation claims the chain reached the contradiction, so its closing step has to be present.

Which side of the graph a method belongs to. Expressible here for the same reason as the rule below: it is an object-internal condition on two of this object's own values, not a relation to a sibling node and not a numeric comparison. The reference states it as prose -- both bindings are used by input nodes only, the checker and the solver by derived and root nodes -- and a reversed pairing describes a check that cannot have happened: a contradiction has no core member to re-encode against, an input has no premises to re-derive from.

The two unit fields travel with the method that admits them, in both directions. Expressible here because it is an object-internal condition on which keys are present; the remaining rule -- unit_index below unit_count -- compares two sibling integers and is a named semantic-gate exception instead.

premise_ids.$comment: Whether an id here names a node, and whether that node comes earlier, are relations between array members.  Draft 2020-12 cannot follow a string to the member it names, so the constructor enforces both.

conclusion.$comment: Fields beyond "kind" depend on the tag and are left open.  One is worth naming: a conclusion about the state a frame holds carries "state_slot": true beside its subject.  A model may declare a variable spelled like that subject -- an import mapping renames past the keyword, and the target-template rule admits "$" -- so the flag, not the spelling, is what tells a consumer whether the conclusion is about a state or about a variable.

verification_method.$comment: No value for an unchecked step: a published proof carries no hole, trust or opaque solver step, so the absence is the contract rather than an omission.

unit_index.$comment: Which requirement of the member's group a core_binding_unit input restates, counting from zero in the group's own decomposition order. Only a core_binding_unit input carries it, and it must be below unit_count.

unit_count.$comment: How many requirements that decomposition has, so a reader sees what proportion of the group one fact covers. Travels with unit_index in both directions: neither may appear without the other, and neither may appear on a whole-group core_binding.

conflictProof.$comment: Graph shape is a semantic-gate exception: node id uniqueness across a nested key, premises naming earlier nodes, a single false root that root_id names, every node reaching that root, input nodes binding one-to-one to core items, and proof.scope equalling core.scope are all relations this schema language cannot express.  The constructor refuses them; validation passing here does not mean the graph is sound.

nodes.$comment: Canonical topological order.  There is no second ordering array; position in this list is the order.
